rounds.text: Brisk Technovision Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 14.6x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of just 5.02x against a sector benchmark of 11.41x [E11]. The underlying profitability and capital efficiency are exceptionally strong, highlighted by an ROCE of 21.7% outperforming the sector benchmark of 11.29% [E10] and a 5-year median return on equity of 26% [E21]. Growth metrics further reinforce this potential, led by a staggering 157% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19] and 18% compounded sales growth over 3 years [E15]. The company also rewards shareholders with a healthy 3.24% dividend yield [E4] and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.15x [E31]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation points to an intrinsic value of Rs 295 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 64.4% [E36, E37], while the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only demands a modest 3.5% earnings growth [E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -1.10 Cr in March 2026 [E29] and three-year compounded profit growth sits at -18% [E18].

A superficial glance at backward-looking metrics masks a severe, alarming collapse in cash generation: operating cash flow for March 2026 plunged into negative territory at Rs -1.10 Cr, dragging cash conversion down to an abysmal -1.08x against reported profit [E28, E29]. Free cash flow followed suit, worsening to Rs -1.82 Cr for the same period [E30]. This cash burn is accompanied by rising borrowings, which climbed to Rs 1.16 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 0.79 Cr a year earlier [E32]. Furthermore, underlying operational profitability is deteriorating, evidenced by TTM operating margins contracting by 3 percentage points to 6% and quarterly margins dropping by 3 percentage points to 5% in September 2026 [E24, E25]. Compounded profit growth over a 3-year horizon tells a dismal story of contraction at -18% [E18], while screen diagnostics explicitly flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E50]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative leverage profile with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.15x and an appealing dividend yield of 3.24% [E4, E31].

The bear highlights negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.10 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -1.82 Cr for March 2026 [E29, E30], but ignores that the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.15x as of September 2026 [E31]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 1.16 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 0.79 Cr a year earlier [E32]. While the bear points to margin contraction [E24, E25] and a 3-year profit contraction of -18% [E18], it dismisses the powerful turnaround currently underway, demonstrated by a massive 157% trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth [E19] and strong recent sales acceleration of 91% year-over-year [E46]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on historical hurdles overlooks the fact that results score a robust 76 out of 100 while current sentiment remains overly cautious [E51]. Finally, the bear's alarm over margin trends ignores the compelling valuation cushion provided by an attractive 3.24% dividend yield [E4] and an EV/EBITDA of 5.02x that trades at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 11.41x [E11].

Conceded: borrowings are a modest Rs 1.16 Cr [E32] and EV/EBITDA sits at 5.02x against a sector benchmark of 11.41x [E11]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash generation risks ignores that operating cash flow is outright negative at Rs -1.10 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs -1.82 Cr for March 2026, resulting in a severe cash conversion ratio of -1.08x [E28, E29, E30]. While the bull points to a 157% trailing twelve-month profit growth figure [E19] and 91% YoY sales acceleration [E46], it glosses over the structural reality of a 3-year compounded profit contraction of -18% [E18]. Furthermore, the bull downplays margin compression, yet operating margins have deteriorated by 3 percentage points both in the TTM comparison and down to 5% in September 2026, accompanied by an inconsistent margin trend [E24, E25, E26, E27]. Finally, citing a 3.24% dividend yield [E4] as valuation support fails to address the underlying cash drain where payouts outpace actual cash generation.
